learning_objective: EASA Part-FCL - ATPL(A) Minimum Flight Experience
stem: Under EASA Part-FCL.510.A, what is the minimum total flight time required for the issuance of an Airline Transport Pilot Licence for aeroplanes [ATPL(A)]?

options.text: 1,500 hours of total flight time, including at least 500 hours in multi-pilot operations and 250 hours as Pilot-in-Command (or 500h PICUS).
1,000 hours of total flight time, including at least 200 hours of instrument time and 100 hours of solo cross-country navigation.
2,000 hours of total flight time, with a minimum of 1,000 hours as Commander on heavy wide-body transport category aircraft.
750 hours of total flight time, provided all training was completed in a certified integrated Multi-Crew Pilot Licence (MPL) cour.

stem: What is the validity period of a multi-engine type rating under EASA Part-FCL, and within what window may it be revalidated by proficiency check?

options.text: Valid for 2 years (24 months); revalidation can be conducted within 6 months prior to expiry with no loss of calendar validity.
Valid for 1 year (12 months); revalidation proficiency check can be conducted within the 3 months immediately preceding the expiry date.
Valid for 6 months; revalidation must be conducted exactly 30 days prior to the expiration date in a Level D simulator.
Valid indefinitely provided the pilot logs at least 10 takeoff and landing sectors every 90 days on the specific aircraft type.

explanation.text:
### Type Rating Validity & Revalidation (FCL.740)
* **Validity:** **1 year (12 calendar months)** from the end of the month of the proficiency check.
* **Revalidation Window:** If completed within the **3 months preceding the expiry date**, the new validity runs for 1 year from the previous expiry date.

stem: What is the validity period of an EASA Class 1 Medical Certificate for commercial pilots under 40 years old vs pilots aged 40 and older in single-pilot operations?

options.text: 24 months for pilots under 40; reduced to 12 months for pilots over 40 regardless of crew composition or commercial operation type.
6 months for all commercial pilots regardless of age, expanding to 12 months only for non-commercial private flying under standard conditions.
12 months for pilots under 40 (and pilots 40-59 in multi-pilot commercial operations); reduced to 6 months for single-pilot ops over 40 or any ops over 60.
60 months for pilots under 30; reduced to 24 months for pilots over 50 and 12 months for pilots over 65 in commercial transport under standard conditions.

explanation.text:
### Class 1 Medical Validity (Part-MED.A.045)
* **Under 40 years:** Valid for **12 months**.
* **40–59 years (Multi-Pilot Commercial CAT):** Valid for **12 months**.
* **40+ years (Single-Pilot Commercial CAT with passengers):** Valid for **6 months**.
* **60+ years (All Commercial CAT):** Valid for **6 months**.

stem: What recent flight experience is mandatory under EASA Part-FCL.060 for a pilot to act as Pilot Flying (PF) on a commercial passenger transport flight?

options.text: At least 10 line sectors and 1 instrument approach within the preceding 60 days on any turbine aircraft type across all applicable operational flight phases.
At least 5 take-offs and landings at night within the preceding 30 days regardless of day flight recency under standard rules.
At least 1 recurrent simulator check within the preceding 45 days in a certified Level D flight training device under standard rules.
At least 3 take-offs, approaches and landings within the preceding 90 days on the same type/class (or in an approved FFS).

explanation.text:
### 90-Day Recency Rule (FCL.060)
* A pilot shall not operate as PIC or co-pilot carrying passengers unless they have carried out in the preceding **90 days** at least **3 take-offs, approaches and landings** as Pilot Flying on the same type/class or in an approved FFS.
* For **night operations as PIC**, at least 1 of the 3 landings must be at night (unless holding an IR).

learning_objective: Operator Proficiency Check (OPC) vs License Proficiency Check (LPC)
stem: Under EASA Part-ORO.FC.230, what is the validity period and required interval for Operator Proficiency Checks (OPC) and Line Checks?

options.text: OPC is valid for 6 calendar months (two checks per year); Line Check is valid for 12 calendar months (conducted on real line routes).
OPC is valid for 12 calendar months; Line Check is valid for 24 calendar months and can be substituted by simulator sessions across all applicable operational flight phases.
OPC is valid for 3 calendar months; Line Check is valid for 6 calendar months and must be conducted by civil authority inspectors.
OPC is valid indefinitely under continuous line flying; Line Check is required only upon initial command upgrade transition under standard rules.

explanation.text:
### OPC and Line Check Requirements (ORO.FC.230)
* **Operator Proficiency Check (OPC):** Valid for **6 calendar months** (operators conduct two simulator checks per year, often combining one with the annual LPC).
* **Line Check:** Valid for **12 calendar months**, verifying normal line operations under commercial conditions.

learning_objective: Age 65 Limitation in Commercial Air Transport
stem: Under EASA Part-FCL.065, what operational limitation applies to a pilot who has attained the age of 60 in commercial air transport operations?

options.text: At age 60, the pilot is immediately restricted to domestic VFR operations only, and all night flying privileges are revoked across all applicable operational flight phases.
Between age 60 and 64, the pilot may only fly in multi-pilot crews where the other pilot is under age 60; at age 65, commercial CAT flying is prohibited.
Between age 60 and 65, the pilot may fly as single-pilot Commander provided they complete monthly medical evaluations under standard rules.
Pilots can continue flying commercial passenger CAT without any age restrictions provided their Class 1 medical is valid under standard rules.

explanation.text:
### Age 60/65 Limitations (FCL.065)
* **Age 60–64:** May act as pilot in commercial air transport **only as a member of a multi-pilot crew** and provided that **the other pilot is under the age of 60**.
* **Age 65:** The holder of a pilot licence shall **not act as a pilot in commercial air transport (CAT)** operations.

learning_objective: UPRT (Upset Prevention and Recovery Training) Mandatory Rule
stem: Under EASA Part-FCL.725.A and FCL.745.A, what is the mandatory requirement for Advanced UPRT for pilots undertaking their first multi-pilot type rating?

options.text: Completion of 10 hours of solo aerobatic flight in an experimental category biplane without theoretical ground school across all applicable operational flight phases during normal flight operations.
Conducting 20 spins in a flight simulator without any requirement for real aeroplane flight training modules under standard rules.
Completion of an Advanced UPRT course according to FCL.745.A (comprising at least 5 hours of theoretical knowledge and 3 hours of on-aeroplane flight instruction).
Passing an oral aerodynamics exam with the national civil aviation authority during initial instrument rating check under standard rules.

explanation.text:
### Advanced UPRT (FCL.745.A)
* Mandatory before commencing the **first multi-pilot type rating course** or single-pilot high performance complex aeroplane type rating.
* Course content: **5 hours of theoretical ground instruction** and **3 hours of flight instruction on an aeroplane** certified for aerobatics/UPRT.

learning_objective: ICAO English Language Proficiency Validity Periods
stem: What are the re-evaluation validity periods for ICAO English Language Proficiency Levels 4, 5, and 6 under EASA Part-FCL.055?

options.text: Level 4 = 2 years; Level 5 = 4 years; Level 6 = 10 years with mandatory written grammar testing at each renewal across all applicable operational flight phases.
Level 4 = 1 year; Level 5 = 3 years; Level 6 = 5 years for all commercial airline transport pilot license holders under standard rules.
All ICAO language levels have 5 years validity and require annual recurrent oral interviews with certified language examiners.
Level 4 (Operational) = 4 years; Level 5 (Extended) = 6 years; Level 6 (Expert) = Permanent validity (no re-evaluation required).

explanation.text:
### ICAO Language Proficiency Validity (FCL.055)
* **Level 4 (Operational):** Valid for **4 years**.
* **Level 5 (Extended):** Valid for **6 years**.
* **Level 6 (Expert):** **Permanent validity** (valid for lifetime of the licence).

learning_objective: Recurrent CRM and Ground Training Cycle (Part-ORO)
stem: Under EASA Part-ORO.FC.220 / 230, what is the mandatory cycle and frequency for operator recurrent ground training and CRM modules?

options.text: All major training topics (CRM, emergency equipment, dangerous goods, security) must be covered over a 3-year recurring cycle, with annual modules.
Ground training is conducted once upon initial hiring and is valid for the duration of employment with no refresher required across all applicable operational flight phases.
CRM training must be repeated every calendar month in an authorized simulator center with video recording under standard rules.
Recurrent ground training is required only if the flight crew changes aircraft type rating or upgrades to command under standard rules.

explanation.text:
### Recurrent Training Cycle (ORO.FC.230)
* Recurrent ground and flight training is structured over a **3-year rolling cycle**.
* Key elements:
  1. **Annual:** Emergency and safety equipment drill, CRM integration, dangerous goods (or 2-year cycle), security.
  2. **Every 3 years:** Complete coverage of all modular CRM syllabus topics, ditching/fire drills, and cold weather ops.

stem: Under EASA CAT.GEN.MPA.105, which of the following emergency powers and legal authorities rests exclusively with the Pilot-in-Command (Commander)?

options.text: Authority to modify national airspace boundaries and reclassify terminal control areas during high traffic congestion across all applicable operational flight phases during normal flight operations.
Authority to give all commands necessary to ensure the safety of the aircraft, persons, and property, and to deviate from rules/procedures in an emergency in the interest of safety.
Authority to cancel airport operational curfews and bypass noise abatement fines without notifying local airport authorities under standard rules.
Authority to issue instant administrative fines to air traffic controllers who refuse preferred direct routing clearances under standard rules.

explanation.text:
### Commander Authority (CAT.GEN.MPA.105)
* The Commander has the **ultimate operational authority** and responsibility for the safety of the aircraft, crew, passengers, and cargo.
* In an **emergency situation** requiring immediate decision and action, the Commander is entitled to **take any action deemed necessary, including deviating from regulations and SOPs**.

stem: Under EASA Part-CAT.GEN.MPA.100 and SERA.2020, what are the strict legal limitations regarding alcohol consumption before flight duty?

options.text: No alcohol within 24 hours prior to departure, and blood alcohol concentration must be below 0.80 per mille (standard driving limit) across all applicable operational flight phases during normal flight operations.
Alcohol consumption is permitted during layovers provided the pilot drinks with food and sleeps at least 4 hours under standard rules.
No alcohol consumption within 8 hours prior to duty reporting, and blood alcohol concentration (BAC) must not exceed 0.20 per mille (0.2 g/l) or operator zero-tolerance policy.
No restrictions apply during domestic repositioning flights with no commercial passengers on board under standard rules.

explanation.text:
### Alcohol Limitations (CAT.GEN.MPA.100 / SERA.2020)
* **Time Limit:** No alcohol consumption within **8 hours** prior to the specified reporting time for flight duty.
* **Blood Alcohol Limit:** Not to exceed **0.20 ‰ (0.2 g/l)** at the start of or during duty.
* NetJets maintains a strict **zero-tolerance** policy regarding psychoactive substances and alcohol on duty.

stem: What is the core philosophy and methodology of Evidence-Based Training (EBT) under EASA Part-ORO.FC.231?

options.text: Requiring pilots to perform all maneuvers exclusively on real aeroplanes without using flight simulators or computer aids across all applicable operational flight phases during normal flight operations.
Conducting flight checks using only written theoretical multiple-choice questionnaires administered via mobile apps under standard rules.
Eliminating all flight evaluations and granting license renewals automatically based on total accumulated flight hours under standard rules.
A paradigm shift from box-ticking maneuvers to developing and assessing core pilot competencies based on comprehensive global airline accident and operational flight data.

explanation.text:
### Evidence-Based Training (EBT) (ORO.FC.231)
* EBT replaces legacy prescriptive testing with **competency-based training** (9 Core Competencies, e.g., Application of Knowledge, Communication, Flight Path Management, Problem Solving, Situational Awareness, Workload Management).
* Scenarios are developed from real operational data and threat environments (CFIT, LOC-I, Weather, System Failures).

learning_objective: Instrument Rating Revalidation Combined with LPC (FCL.625)
stem: If an Instrument Rating (IR) is revalidated through a proficiency check combined with a multi-pilot type rating (LPC), what cross-credit rules apply?

options.text: Passing the multi-pilot type rating LPC fulfills all IR revalidation requirements for that specific multi-pilot type rating.
The pilot must perform a separate 2-hour single-engine piston flight test to maintain the multi-engine instrument rating across all applicable operational flight phases.
The IR is revalidated for 6 months only, while the type rating is revalidated for 24 calendar months under standard rules.
Cross-crediting between type ratings and instrument ratings is strictly prohibited under European FCL regulations under standard rules.

explanation.text:
### IR Revalidation Cross-Crediting (FCL.625.A & Appendix 8)
* When an IR(A) proficiency check is combined with an **operator proficiency check (OPC) or licence proficiency check (LPC)** on a multi-pilot type rating in an approved FFS, passing the check **revalidates the IR privileges** for that type.

learning_objective: High Altitude Endorsement / High Altitude Training (FCL.720.A)
stem: What theoretical and practical training is required before a pilot operates a pressurised aeroplane capable of operating above FL250?

options.text: Completion of a 50-hour celestial navigation sextant plotting course and high-latitude compass deviation calculations across all applicable operational flight phases.
High altitude physiology, hypoxia awareness, cabin decompression profiles, emergency descent procedures, and rapid don oxygen mask drills.
Hypobaric chamber explosive decompression testing at zero pressure altitude every 6 calendar months under standard rules.
Obtaining a specialized military high-altitude interceptor rating issued by national defense authorities under standard rules.

explanation.text:
### High Altitude Training (FCL.720.A / Part-SPA)
* Prior to operating above **FL250**, pilots must complete **High Altitude Training** covering:
  1. Physiological hazards of high altitude and **hypoxia** symptoms.
  2. **Time of Useful Consciousness (TUC)** at various flight levels.
  3. Rapid cabin depressurisation mechanics.
  4. **Emergency Descent** execution and emergency oxygen equipment donning.

stem: Under EASA Part-MED.A.020, under what medical circumstances is a pilot legally obliged to suspend flying and notify the Aeromedical Examiner (AME)?

options.text: Any minor headache lasting more than 30 minutes during a scheduled layover rest period at an outstation across all applicable operational flight phases during normal flight operations.
Changing spectacle prescription by less than 0.25 diopters without changes in visual acuity under standard rules.
Hospital admission > 12h, surgical operation, ongoing medication use, significant personal injury, pregnancy, or medical illness incapacity > 21 days.
Only when the civil aviation authority issues a formal written grounded order following a ramp inspection under standard rules.
